issues.description: signing_mode_enum branches on (is_hex, safe_mode) are not exhaustive and silently rely on a fall-through default
issues.detail: The helper handles three of four boolean combinations with if/elif and lets the fourth (is_hex=False, safe_mode=True) fall through to the final return. State the invariant explicitly: enumerate all four cases and use a match or full if/elif/else so the mapping is provable from inspection. As written, a reader cannot verify completeness without truth-tabling it.

issues.description: sign_message and verify_signature duplicate the mode->message-bytes encoding instead of sharing one canonical routine
issues.detail: Both functions reimplement the SigningMode dispatch that produces the bytes actually signed/verified. This is exactly the kind of duplication that lets sign and verify drift: a future contributor could fix one branch and miss the other. Extract a single `message_bytes_for_mode(mode, message) -> bytes` and call it from both sides; the invariant 'verify reverses sign' becomes textual, not coincidental.

issues.description: verify_signature docstring is stale boilerplate (':param request:') for a function that no longer takes a request
issues.detail: The function was lifted out of the RPC handler verbatim, including its ':param request: :return:' docstring, but the signature is now keyword-only fields. For a newly created library module this is precisely the place literate-programming discipline matters: state inputs, outputs, and the address-binding invariant (puzzle_hash must equal expected_puzzle_hash for non-None address) in prose.

issues.description: Variable name `hex_message` is now misleading since it holds tree-hash bytes or utf-8 bytes, not hex
issues.detail: Inside sign_message the local is called hex_message but in three of four branches it is not a hex-derived value; one branch holds a Program tree hash, another holds utf-8 bytes. The name was inherited from the old wallet method. Rename to `message_to_sign` (mirroring verify_signature's `message_to_verify`) so the symmetry between sign and verify is visible to the reader.

issues.description: convert_secret_key_to_synthetic is an instance method that uses no instance state
issues.detail: Wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic takes self but only forwards to calculate_synthetic_secret_key with the module-level DEFAULT_HIDDEN_PUZZLE_HASH. Either make it @staticmethod (or a module function in util/signing) so callers do not have to route through main_wallet, or document why instance binding is load-bearing. As written it adds an indirection the reader has to chase.

issues.description: test_sign_message_by_address does not assert isValid on the verify response
issues.detail: The new test calls verify_signature but never asserts the returned VerifySignatureResponse.isValid is True. Since verify_signature returns a response object (not raising), a regression that makes every signature fail verification would still let this test pass. Bind the result and assert response.isValid is True; tests catch what proofs miss only when they actually check the postcondition.

review.summary: The refactor is a sensible consolidation: ad-hoc sign_message methods on Wallet, DIDWallet, and NFTWallet are replaced by a util module plus current_p2_puzzle_hash helpers, and the RPC handler shrinks accordingly. The algorithmic content is unchanged, which is the right kind of refactor. The rigor gaps are mostly literate-programming: the new util module inherits a stale docstring and a misleading local name, the (is_hex, safe_mode) mapping is encoded as a non-exhaustive if/elif chain, and the encode-mode-to-bytes logic is duplicated between sign and verify rather than extracted as the shared invariant it actually is. The new NFT-id test is thorough across modes; the new address test forgets to assert the verify postcondition. UNDER-AUDITED, with NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on chia/wallet/util/signing.py.
